harnesses.name: terminal_input::utf16::proofs::native_key_phase_preserves_alt_text_and_ordinary_releases

harnesses.input_domain: Every i32 down fact, u16 repeat count, virtual key and Unicode unit, and u32 modifier mask.

harnesses.name: terminal_input::utf16::proofs::every_alt_text_scalar_survives_interleaved_zero_unit_modifiers

harnesses.input_domain: Every valid nonzero Rust char encoded into one or two UTF-16 units, with the actual four-record ConPTY Alt-text schedule for supplementary scalars.
harnesses.bound: Unwind 6 with unwinding assertions; complete scalar range through the real production record decoder, without a general OS scheduling theorem.
harnesses.production: platform::terminal::windows passes checked native WindowsKey facts into the same Utf16Decoder::windows_key; the native ConPTY trace reproduced this Alt key-up surrogate schedule and retains the required emoji assertion.

harnesses.name: terminal_input::unicode::proofs::only_canonical_utf8_sequences_admit_a_scalar

harnesses.input_domain: Every four-byte array and every complete sequence length two through four.
harnesses.bound: Unwind 6 with unwinding assertions; byte-level canonical admission combined with the independent all-scalar production decoder roundtrip. Rust char and encoder semantics remain language verifier contracts.
harnesses.production: terminal_input::Decoder::utf8 calls this same checked unicode::scalar on its actual bounded complete sequence content before publishing a KeyEvent.

harnesses.name: terminal_input::sequence::proofs::every_sequence_append_preserves_its_buffer_invariant
harnesses.contract: The only production sequence mutators admit exactly one byte while capacity remains, preserve every other array slot, refuse full buffers unchanged, and clear to an empty bounded sequence.
harnesses.input_domain: Every 32-byte buffer, every admitted usize length zero through 32, every appended byte and every array coordinate zero through 31.
harnesses.bound: Unwind 34 with unwinding assertions; constructor and actual append/clear induction, with private fields preventing decoder counter assignment. This does not prove every arbitrary-length keyboard sequence has its intended semantic event.
harnesses.production: terminal_input::Decoder owns private Sequence, accesses only its checked content, and calls these actual push and clear methods for UTF-8 and CSI input.

boundaries.reason: The source-bound scalar decisions do not establish redb durability, peer origin authentication, local actor binding, immutable event storage or output-stream completion. Dedicated metadata indexes are derived atomically from admitted actual handoff events and body lookup occurs only after the production descriptor admission.
boundaries.evidence: Native handoff fixtures cover body-corrupt metadata discovery, denied-reader body-port nonreachability, actual-reader observation and transaction rollback, foreign-peer omission, previous-inbox denial, own-identity scoped continuation, all three prior store formats and identity reset. Actual MCP serve_io and completion fixtures inject payload/newline/flush faults, before/during-flush cancellation, oversized-result substitution, global actor rebound and ungranted same-name identity; only the original successfully flushed uncancelled body commits its bound actual-reader observation.
boundaries.reconsider: Peer trust or local identity admission changes, a native metadata/body or output/commit ordering fixture fails, or a supported verifier models the actual database and external stream boundary.

boundaries.reason: The source-bound decision and counted-port proofs do not establish PowerShell compilation time, filesystem publication, monotonic-clock scheduling, windows-spawn creation-time Job attachment, or Win32 accounting/termination. A retained fresh Job is attached during process creation before PowerShell can launch compiler children; the original native reader and binary channels are unchanged.
boundaries.evidence: The dedicated input_controller target controls preparation6s then live Ready/completion7s, exact operation5s and whole-case180s boundaries, foreign/malformed/disappeared readiness, regressed clocks, and primary-plus-cleanup faults through the actual controller. The Windows bootstrap scenario preserves all eight actual input schedules and adds a known held Rust descendant observed inside its creation-time Job, exact operation refusal, retained root reap, and zero active processes before capture. No original hosted failure cause is inferred from successful reruns.
boundaries.reconsider: A phase/channel, Job attachment, accounting, ownership, cleanup, or native deadline contract changes or fails, or a verifier supports the actual Win32/CLR boundary.

boundaries.reason: The actual admission transition depends on filesystem identity, private candidate ACLs, operating-system selection/usage locks, directory publication, and the publisher-to-node lifetime. The segmented writer proof cannot establish these effects. Selection bridges publication to final usage admission because Windows refuses renaming a directory with open child-file handles.
boundaries.evidence: Native builds::tests on each supported host check a legacy exposed parent's protected candidate, a separate pruner blocked after publication until final usage admission, existing-winner and losing-installer admission, invalid/link refusal, and usage retained through the actual first-node callback. The original two-idle retention policy remains; fixtures make the candidate eligible using two newer idle companions. Replacement fixtures preserve the destination and recreated names and remove only an empty outer stage.
boundaries.reconsider: A native publication, selection, usage, identity, or cleanup contract fails, filesystem or locking semantics change, or the first-node ownership protocol changes.

boundaries.reason: Kani verifies the actual bounded Rust segmented writer, not CLR pinning/marshalling, PowerShell stdin inheritance, or overlapped Win32 completion semantics. The prefix reader retains its borrowed pipe handle, pinned bytes, event, and operation until native completion.
boundaries.evidence: The source-bound native Windows bootstrap scenario runs the actual script in Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7, eight SDK inherited-overlapped-input schedules with exact binary prefix/remainder/EOF, and refusal without publication for truncated input, a write-only handle, and a failed pending observer. All hosts exercise the exact original frame, snapshot digest and bytes, isolated installer input/output, one upload/first-request connection, and primary-preserving cwd/cleanup faults.
boundaries.reconsider: The actual reader, shell launcher, byte-mode pipe assumption, FFI lifetime, source prefix format, or any native handoff contract changes.

boundaries.reason: The source-bound scalar budget/read-length, finite ASCII metadata, and bounded actual std::path proofs do not establish native Git configuration and path output, canonical directory identity and case folding, declaration stability, ignore matching, concurrent mutation, capability-relative file opening, Windows reparse semantics, or tar publication. The actual source adapter captures canonical Git/common directories through individually bounded queries before top-level discovery, refuses selected metadata/bare roots or unresolved declarations, and excludes both trees after canonicalization from the merged tracked and walker paths. Git's bounded untracked-path query owns Git-ignore precedence; the walker retains .ignore and no-follow entry policy. One retained selected-root capability owns archive admission.
boundaries.evidence: Native source, source_archive, source_fingerprint and source_file tests cover Git-written global excludes paths with spaces and inherited config-count context, ignored tracked modified bytes, ignored untracked exclusion, deletion, real .GIT metadata, and subdirectory paths. Actual Git oracle fixtures cover ancestor-ignored exclusion, competing relative excludes files, repository-root anchored patterns, and separate-directory info/exclude precedence with .gitignore negation. Separate, distinct common, forced-tracked metadata and nested-selection controls require only current working bytes; malformed ancestor declarations, selected metadata/bare roots, and unresolved case aliases refuse, while valid symlink/case aliases are bound to actual canonical directories and non-Git HEAD/objects working names remain ordinary input. Finite Miri controls bind Path::components to the actual typed matcher for whole components and rooted/relative namespaces. Shared runtime/build readers retain every captured parent; Unix uses public cap-primitives open_dir_nofollow and safe rustix NOFOLLOW|NONBLOCK|CLOEXEC, while Windows NtCreateFile uses RootDirectory and OPEN_REPARSE_POINT for every component, rejecting non-disk/reparse handles before reads. Native controls replace inspected parents/final files, rename captured ancestors/root names, refuse a writerless FIFO within a killed/reaped child deadline, preserve read errors, and bound growth/truncation reads to admitted length+1. Native parser tests admit exactly MAX_PATH_BYTES in complete valid records and refuse one extra path byte separately from stream/count/record limits. Native case folding, custom bare identification without Git or an explicit declaration, and one atomic view of concurrently modified Git state/files are not claimed.
boundaries.reconsider: Git output, ancestor ignore semantics, or capability/filesystem semantics change, a native source, link, budget, collision or archive contract fails, or a verifier can check the actual Git/filesystem adapter boundary.

boundaries.reason: The source-bound ordered request-port and bounded Write-port proofs do not establish actual JSON decoding, native Unix socket EOF or timeout causes, launchd, descriptor inheritance, concurrency, or every possible port implementation.
boundaries.evidence: The mandatory Mac workspace tests exercise actual bounded ingress decoding and Handoff validation, tagged Read/Decode/Validate/Launch refusals, an actual partial-request timeout with zero launches, injected partial-read WouldBlock retaining native error kind/code/cause, and complete readiness/refusal through UnixStream with a held receiver clone. The core handoff Miri lane interprets the same ordered request function; the cross-platform login_reply target and its Miri lane import the production write/shutdown adapter. Passing reruns do not identify the original intermittent refusal's cause.
boundaries.reconsider: Reply framing or socket semantics change, a native integration fails, or a verifier supports the actual concurrent operating-system boundary.

boundaries.reason: The finite protocol step and job-state proofs do not establish filesystem locking, worker creation, SSH reliability, or native process lifetime.
boundaries.evidence: Native workspace tests exercise duplicate and conflicting submission, the existing launch-lock boundary, finished-job retries, launch refusal, and missing-supervisor state through the production app and Store adapters.
boundaries.reconsider: The launch or store locking protocol changes, a native adapter contract fails, or a verifier supports the actual filesystem and process boundary.

boundaries.reason: The supported native Kani, Quint/Apalache, Miri, and libFuzzer owner lane runs on Linux and Mac; native Windows verifier capability is not claimed.
boundaries.evidence: Linux or Mac: mise run verify and mise run miri on the exact source digest; Windows: cargo xtask verify inventory, cargo xtask windows-contracts, and mise run test for native SDK, process ownership, and filesystem contracts.
boundaries.reconsider: A pinned native verifier supports Windows, the implementation adds target-specific core decisions, or any native Windows contract fails.

boundaries.reason: Kani does not establish concurrent Win32 kernel ownership or foreign-function behavior.
boundaries.evidence: mise x -- cargo xtask windows-contracts; mise run test on Windows exercises capability, child ownership, failure cleanup, and process-tree termination.
boundaries.reconsider: A verifier supports the actual Win32 boundary, SDK semantics change, or a native ownership contract fails.

boundaries.reason: Source-bound receipt, stop, deadline, activity and byte-admission proofs do not establish redb durability, peer origin authentication, native locking, clock synchronization or client consumption. The actual ledger projections and fallback link share a single redb transaction, while hook output and its delivered receipt are separate resources.
boundaries.evidence: Native chat store fixtures exercise recipient-scoped delivery/read/ack synchronization, distinct room recipients, exact deadlines, one-time fallback and previous-format identity/history preservation. Actual backend faults refuse receipt writes and check old-or-complete-new atomic state after sync errors, with idempotent retry; counter exhaustion rolls back escalation before replay. Hook and CLI fixtures retain bounded context, urgent stop, subsequent-action reading, status/presence and failed output leaving new delivery pending.
boundaries.reconsider: A receipt, deadline, output/commit, identity or native durability fixture fails, a supported client exposes a causal consumption receipt, or a verifier checks the actual database, client or stream boundary.

boundaries.reason: The source-bound finite compaction and capture-policy proofs do not establish all JSON document shapes, filesystem writes, native client scheduling, hook trust or operating-system stream behavior. Setup requires complete structured readiness output and preserves foreign hooks; it never writes native trust hashes.
boundaries.evidence: Native setup fixtures preserve malformed prior hook bytes exactly, retain owner stop groups, check idempotent merge and read-only diagnosis, and refuse failed registration adds, mismatched post-add registration and nonzero credential queries. Provider fixtures bind all four phases, literal platform executable paths and --if-bound without a Codex trust bypass. Actual capture fixtures require exact-budget output, refuse drained overflow, retain read errors and preserve nonzero native outcomes.
boundaries.reconsider: The supported client schema, lifecycle or native trust semantics change, a configuration/capture/readiness fixture fails, or a verifier checks the actual client or native filesystem boundary.
